business.description: Wanbury Limited is a pharmaceutical company with manufacturing plants at Patalganga (Maharashtra) and Tanuku (Andhra Pradesh).

products.name: Wanbury C RED
products.note: Next-generation Liposomal Iron formulation for anemia management, launched regionally in India.

products.name: Coriminic CPM Drops
products.note: Chlorpheniramine Maleate drops for pediatric usage, launched to address DCGI restrictions on fixed-dose combinations in children under 4 years.

products.name: Coriminic NS Nasal Drops
products.note: Normal Saline nasal drops for localized relief from nasal congestion in children.

products.name: Sertraline

outlook.statement: High-Demand Anaesthetic API – Production Ramp-Up Signals Rapid Growth Ahead
Sertraline Form II approval from ANVISA will help further consolidate company's share of business in Brazil
GMP certificate from TGA (Australia) once received will enable Wanbury to ship additional 3 APIs
New SAP S/4HANA ERP system will serve as a scalable platform to support the Company's future growth initiatives

For the API business, sustain growth momentum through commercialisation of new molecules (targeting approximately four launches per year beginning FY 2026-27), continued brownfield capacity expansion, and further borrowing-cost optimisation.

For the formulations business, move from turnaround and break-even (targeted in FY 2025-26) to rebuilding and scale-up in FY 2026-27, with a shift in portfolio mix towards speciality and chronic-therapy segments, alongside continued brand-building in Coriminic and C-RED.

risks: No element of risk which in opinion of the Board threatens the existence of the Company
Highly competitive environment with pricing as key success factor
Regulatory compliance risks with stricter global regulators (USFDA, etc.)
Export and geopolitical risk (majority revenue export-oriented, exposed to regional disruptions, forex volatility, shipping/logistics constraints)
Leverage and refinancing risk (term debt Rs. 215.45 crore as of 31st March 2026, sensitive to interest-rate and refinancing conditions)

The Company is exposed to foreign exchange risks emanating from the business, assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currency. In order to hedge this risk, the Company proactively uses hedging instruments e.g., forward contracts, options and other simple derivatives from time to time.

Investment Risk: For funded plans that rely on insurers for managing the assets, the value of assets certified by the insurer may not be the fair value of instruments backing the liability

Liquidity Risk: Employees with high salaries and long durations or those higher in hierarchy, accumulate significant level of benefits. If some of such employees resign/retire from the Company there can be strain on the cashflows

Legislative Risk: Legislative risk is the risk of increase in the plan liabilities or reduction in the plan assets due to change in the legislation/regulation
